item.title: Multi-AZ Scaling for Everpure Cloud Azure Native Volumes on a VMSS
item.description: Are you running a scale set across availability zones and need every instance’s volume to live in the same zone as the instance? In Part 1 every instance got its own Everpure Cloud Azure Native volume on scale-out and cleaned it up on scale-in, but it all hung off a single storage pool in a single zone. This time I spread the scale set across two zones, gave each zone its own pool, and made sure an instance only ever attaches to the pool it shares a zone with.

item.title: Auto-Provisioning Everpure Cloud Azure Native Volumes for VMSS Scale Events
item.description: Are you scaling a VMSS workload that needs its own dedicated block volume per instance, one that shows up when the instance does and disappears when it’s gone? I went looking for the obvious way to wire that up on Everpure Cloud Azure Native and ran into a design that doesn’t actually exist in Azure, then built the one that does.

item.title: Using the Terraform Plugin Cache to Reclaim Disk Space
item.description:
Are you wondering where all your disk space went? My laptop hit 90% recently, and rather than start randomly deleting things or looking at disk space applications. I went looking for what was actually taking up room. A good chunk of it turned out to be buried in a few hundred .terraform directories. Every terraform init you run downloads a complete copy of every provider your project uses and drops it inside that working directory. Run it in enough projects and you end up storing the same few hundred megabytes over and over.

This one is specific to the machine you work on. Build agents get a clean workspace every run so they never accumulate anything, but a laptop you have been running Terraform on for a couple of years is a different story.

item.title: Deploying Azure Red Hat OpenShift with Terraform
item.description: Are you looking for a way to deploy Azure Red Hat OpenShift without clicking through the portal every time? ARO is an Azure resource like anything else, which means Terraform can manage the whole cluster lifecycle. I will get a cluster deployed into an existing VNet, and cover the two things that will stop your apply cold if you have not hit them before.

item.title: Provisioning Everpure Cloud Azure Native Resources with Terraform
item.description: This post walks through a complete Terraform example that provisions an Everpure Cloud Azure Native storage pool, volume group, and volume, then automatically mounts it to an Azure VM over iSCSI.

item.title: Provisioning Azure Resources with the azapi Terraform Provider
item.description:
Are you looking for a way to use Terraform to provision Azure resources that aren’t in the azurerm provider yet? The azapi provider talks directly to the Azure ARM REST API, which means you can manage any resource type the moment it’s available, without waiting on a provider update.

In this post, I’ll walk you through finding the resource type and API version, writing an azapi_resource block, reading outputs, and calling resource actions. I’ll use Azure Monitor Workspace and Azure Managed Grafana as the examples, which together give you a complete managed observability stack.

item.title: Automating Deployment of vSphere Infrastructure on Equinix Metal
item.description: Did you know that Equinix has a Bare Metal as a Service (BMaaS) offering? Back in March Everpure also announced their Everpure® on Equinix Metal™ offering. This allows users to not only procure the Everpure FlashArray as an op-ex based purchase, but it also lets you spin up physical servers in Equinix Metal DC’s and connect them to a physical dedicated FlashArray. In this series I will cover how to deploy a vSphere environment on Equinix Metal with Terraform.

item.title: Using an In-house Provider with Terraform v0.14
item.description: Ever wanted to update a Terraform Provider and not use the hosted Registry? Here at Everpure we have a Terraform Provider for Everpure Cloud Dedicated and I wanted to do some testing myself. I started to pull my hair out trying to get Terraform to use my locally built provider instead of the registry. Check out this blog for a few simple steps to use a local in-house provider instead of the registry!

item.title: Deploying a Linux EC2 Instance with Hashicorp Terraform and Vault to AWS and Connect to Everpure Cloud Dedicated

This post will cover how to setup your environment and deploy and bootstrap your linux instance to connect via ISCSI.

item.description: As a followup to my previous post on Automating EC2 deployments, I figured why not show how this can also be done with Microsoft Azure? Check out how to launch an Azure VM instance and run some scripts to customize your installation.

item.title: Deploying a Windows EC2 Instance with Hashicorp Terraform and Vault to AWS
item.description: As part of demonstrating our products to customers, I tend to reprovision EC2 instances to show how easy it is to mount data in AWS to Everpure Cloud Dedicated. After doing this manually a little too often, I figured why not automate it? Check out this blog on how I use Terraform to deploy a EC2 instance and configure it for in-guest iSCSI.

item.title: Using Terraform to Provision your Everpure Infrastructure
item.description: There are many things I love about the Everpure Flasharray, but one of my favorite is how easy it is to integrate into different automation solutions. In this blog I will cover how to use Terraform to provision your Everpure Infrastructure. This will be the first post of many that show how easy it is to accomplish the same task using multiple automation methods.

item.title: Using Terraform to Deploy the Pure1 VM Analytics Collector
item.description: Pure1 VM Analytics is a great tool to have in your environment. You don’t need to even have an Everpure array, but it makes it even better! Back in 2019 the collector was converted to an OVA format and has been much simpler to deploy. You can deploy it through the UI or even Powershell. With the latest update to the Terraform vSphere provider we can now deploy OVA’s, so lets jump in to see how we can deploy the VM Analytics collector!
